messages.text:
"MUSIC EMPIRE – Major Expansion & Visual Upgrade

Expand the existing Music Empire game by adding the following five interconnected features. Integrate everything into the current game, preserving all existing systems, progress, artists, finances and gameplay.

1. BUILD YOUR OWN STUDIO COMPLEX

- Build and upgrade multiple recording studios, production rooms, songwriting rooms, offices and executive suites.
- Each building should have different upgrade levels, visual appearances and functionality.
- Hire producers, sound engineers, songwriters and other music professionals.
- Better facilities and staff should improve music quality, production speed and artist satisfaction.
- Introduce interactive 3D studio environments, including recording booths, microphones, mixing desks, speakers, instruments, furniture and studio equipment.
- Allow players to view and customise their studio interiors.

2. MUSIC LEGACY & COLLECTORS COLLECTION

- Collect gold records, platinum records, diamond certifications and legendary album awards.
- Display iconic album covers, signed records, special edition vinyl, tour posters and artist memorabilia.
- Successful releases should unlock physical awards and collectibles.
- Create a dedicated Hall of Fame and trophy room that players can customise and expand.
- Include rare collectible items with different rarity levels.
- Display collections inside visually detailed 3D environments with shelves, display cabinets, walls and trophy stands.

3. ANNUAL MUSIC AWARDS

- Introduce Artist of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Best New Artist and Best Producer.
- Artists from every record label should compete, including AI-controlled competitors.
- Determine nominations and winners using actual in-game performance, popularity, streams, sales and critical reception.
- Host annual award ceremonies with animated presentations, trophies and celebrations.
- Winning awards should increase artist reputation, popularity and commercial value.
- Keep historical award records and previous winners.
- Include a visually impressive 3D awards venue and stage.

4. CREATE YOUR OWN MUSIC FESTIVAL

- Choose your festival name, branding, location and theme.
- Build stages, VIP areas, food courts, merchandise stalls and backstage facilities.
- Book signed artists and negotiate appearances from external artists.
- Create festival lineups and manage performance schedules.
- Set ticket prices, sponsorship deals and advertising campaigns.
- Introduce attendance, crowd satisfaction, expenses and profit calculations.
- Expand from small local festivals into massive international music events.
- Include detailed 3D festival environments, stages, crowds, lighting, speakers and performance areas.

5. LIVING ARTISTS & EVOLVING MUSIC CAREERS

Make artists feel like real people with evolving careers rather than static characters.

- Every artist should have unique personalities, ambitions, strengths, weaknesses and musical preferences.
- Artists should gain or lose popularity depending on releases, performances, controversies and industry trends.
- Introduce relationships, rivalries, friendships and collaborations.
- Artists can become superstars, struggle commercially, take breaks, change genres or experience career comebacks.
- Introduce contract negotiations, royalty disagreements, creative differences and potential label departures.
- Artists can leave and establish their own independent labels, becoming competitors.
- Introduce artist ageing, career stages, retirement and legacy status.
- Allow players to develop undiscovered talent into international superstars.
- AI record labels should actively discover, sign, promote and manage competing artists.
- Artist decisions and career developments should happen dynamically over time.

6. VISUAL STYLE & MOBILE GRAPHICS – VERY IMPORTANT

Use a hybrid 2D and 3D visual style designed specifically for mobile devices.

2D interface and menus:

- Keep the main game navigation, dashboards, menus, management screens, statistics, charts and buttons in a clean, modern 2D mobile interface.
- Use polished layouts, clear typography, attractive panels and intuitive navigation.
- Menus should feel like a premium mobile tycoon game, not a complicated desktop management simulator.

3D icons and visual elements:

- Use attractive 3D-rendered icons throughout the interface.
- Buildings, studio equipment, records, trophies, microphones, headphones, instruments and other important objects should have detailed 3D appearances.
- Use subtle shadows, depth, lighting and animations to make the interface feel modern and premium.
- Avoid generic flat placeholder icons wherever a 3D visual would improve the experience.

3D environments and interactive spaces:
Certain areas of the game must have actual 3D environments rather than simply displaying static 2D images.

Examples include:

- Recording studios with visible rooms, recording booths, microphones, mixing consoles, speakers and instruments.
- Office interiors with desks, computers, furniture and staff.
- Collectors' rooms with 3D display cabinets, signed records, trophies and memorabilia.
- Music festival grounds with 3D stages, crowds, lighting and backstage areas.
- Award ceremony venues with 3D stages and presentation areas.

Allow players to view these environments, with smooth camera movement and appropriate interactions where possible.

Mobile optimisation:

- Optimise all 3D models, textures, lighting and animations for mobile performance.
- Ensure smooth gameplay, fast loading and efficient memory usage.
- Maintain a consistent visual identity throughout all screens and environments.
- Use portrait-friendly layouts where appropriate, with landscape support where useful.

DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS

- Integrate all new systems into the existing game.
- Do not rebuild or remove existing mechanics.
- Ensure all new features are functional and connected to the existing economy, artists, progression and reputation systems.
- Avoid decorative features that do nothing.
- Prioritise actual gameplay functionality alongside visual improvements.
- Maintain existing save data and player progression.

The overall result should feel like a premium mobile music industry tycoon: clean 2D management menus, beautiful 3D icons and detailed 3D environments for the most important parts of the music business."

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand Music Empire with interconnected studio, collectibles, awards, festivals, and evolving-artist systems.
- Deliver a polished, mobile-first management game with interactive 3D-style environments while preserving the existing game and player progress.

## Requirements
- Integrate features with the existing economy, progression, artists, AI labels, reputation, and saves; preserve existing mechanics, progress, artists, and finances.
- Support studio construction, upgrades, staff, and customization; music legacy collectibles; awards; festivals; and evolving artist careers.
- Make features functional, save-compatible, and optimized for mobile, with interactive environments and no purely decorative mechanics.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing vanilla JavaScript app and data model rather than rebuilding it.
- Use dependency-free SVG icons and a lightweight canvas renderer for environments.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added expansion datasets, artist profile helpers, pseudo-3D SVG icons, and canvas scenes.
- Integrated studio upgrades/design, collectibles and certifications, awards seasons/ceremonies, festivals, artist career evolution, artist meetings, and event outcomes.
- Added navigation, dashboard entry points, feature views, ceremony/festival modals, and action handlers.
- Added responsive styling and fixed scene rendering issues.
- Browser-tested new-label startup, studio upgrades/design, collectibles display, awards ceremony/history, festival creation/upgrades, legacy-save migration, and mobile layout; mobile overflow check passed.

### Active
- Audit remaining game/UI logic, especially festival booking and lifecycle, save compatibility, and artist career-event behavior.
- Run final syntax/runtime checks and inspect browser errors and responsive screenshots.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect test output and screenshots under `/tmp/opencode/`; rerun browser checks for festival booking and lifecycle.
2. Run `node --check` across changed JavaScript files and review the diff for undefined symbols, inconsistent state fields, or regressions.
3. Confirm save migration and mobile layouts across feature views; summarize verification and limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: State migration, persistence, economy, simulation, and expansion systems.
- `js/ui.js`: Navigation, feature views, modals, and action handlers.
- `js/data.js`: Feature datasets and artist/event definitions.
- `js/scene3d.js`: Interactive canvas environments and scene controls.
- `js/visuals.js`: Dependency-free pseudo-3D SVG icons.
- `css/styles.css`: Responsive styling for the expanded interface.
- `js/app.js`: Browser initialization and save startup.
- `index.html`: App entry and module loading.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing save key is `music-empire-save-v1`; browser checks verified expansion fields migrate onto a stripped legacy save.
- Browser screenshots: `/tmp/opencode/v3-studio.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/v3-legacy.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/v3-awards.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/v3-festivals.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/v3-dashboard.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/v3-mobile-studio.jpg`.
- Latest browser check confirmed scene geometry rendered in studio, legacy, awards, and festival views; mobile scene measured 352×300 with no horizontal overflow.

21: ## 🎧 Music Empire — Music Industry Tycoon
22: 
23: A complete, browser-based label management sim. Start with $150K, a bedroom studio and no artists. Scout talent, cut records, fight for chart positions, run campaigns and tours, buy out rivals and build the biggest label in the world.
24: 
25: ### Play
26: 
27: ```bash
28: python3 -m http.server 3002
29: ```
30: 
31: Open <http://localhost:3002>. No build step, accounts or dependencies — the whole game is vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and it saves automatically to `localStorage`.
32: 
33: ### What's inside
34: 
35: - **Roster & talent** — scouting reports, contract negotiation, morale, loyalty, royalties, renewals and rival poaching.

- Expand Music Empire into a polished, mobile-first management game with interconnected studio, collectibles, awards, festivals, and evolving-artist systems.
- Preserve existing mechanics and player progress while keeping the vanilla JavaScript app and save-compatible data model.

## Requirements
- Integrate with the existing economy, progression, artists, AI labels, reputation, and saves.
- Use dependency-free SVG icons and lightweight canvas environments.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing app rather than rebuilding it.
- Preserve and migrate legacy saves by adding expansion fields.

- Integrated feature navigation, dashboard entry points, views, modals, action handlers, and responsive styling.

The save-restoration failure was in the audit procedure, not evidence that the game save had changed. Reloading fired the app’s `beforeunload` handler, which saved the audit’s mutated in-memory state over the restored save. The check also relied on exact serialization, which can differ even when parsed save data is unchanged.

I updated `/tmp/opencode/festival-audit.mjs` to restore the saved data in both localStorage and game state, then compare parsed data. The check now passes: no top-level save values changed, and the original week, cash, and festival count are preserved.

The festival lifecycle audit also passed: completion and poster reward worked, the artist’s popularity and morale updated, post-completion booking and upgrades were rejected, and there were no runtime errors. The earlier smoke checks covered all feature screens and mobile layout without reported horizontal overflow.

Final `node --check` and `git diff --check` passed. No repository files were changed during this audit follow-up; the existing six modified or untracked implementation files remain as noted.

messages.text:
"MUSIC EMPIRE – Entertainment Industry Expansion

Expand the existing Music Empire game by introducing four major interconnected systems. Build everything into the current game without removing, replacing or breaking existing features, artists, finances or player progression.

1. MUSIC PUBLISHING COMPANY

Allow the player to establish and operate their own music publishing division.

- Sign songwriters, composers and independent music creators.
- Purchase, manage and own music publishing catalogues.
- Acquire song copyrights and publishing rights.
- Earn royalties whenever owned songs are streamed, performed, broadcast, licensed or used by other artists.
- Allow other record labels and independent artists to license songs from your catalogue.
- Introduce royalty splits, publishing agreements, licensing fees and copyright negotiations.
- Allow signed artists to write and register their own songs.
- Track individual song earnings, catalogue value and lifetime royalties.
- Introduce valuable legendary music catalogues that can be purchased or sold.
- Build a dedicated publishing department with upgradeable offices and staff.

Make publishing a long-term business that generates recurring income even when the player is focusing on other activities.

2. MUSIC VIDEO PRODUCTION COMPANY

Allow the player to establish a professional music video production studio.

- Hire directors, cinematographers, editors, creative directors and production crews.
- Produce music videos for your signed artists and external clients.
- Choose video concepts, locations, budgets, production quality and visual styles.
- Introduce different video categories, including low-budget clips, professional music videos, cinematic productions and blockbuster productions.
- Build and upgrade filming studios, sound stages, editing suites and production facilities.
- Invest in cameras, lighting, sets, props and special effects.
- Video quality, creativity, artist popularity and marketing should influence the video's success.
- Successful videos should increase streams, followers, song popularity and artist reputation.
- Allow videos to go viral or completely underperform.
- Introduce video views, audience engagement, production expenses and profits.
- Allow the company to produce music videos for competing labels and independent artists for additional income.

Include detailed 3D production environments, filming equipment, sets and interactive studio spaces.

3. RECORD LABEL ACQUISITIONS & CORPORATE EXPANSION

Introduce a complete system for acquiring, merging and managing competing record labels.

- Generate multiple AI-controlled record labels with unique names, branding, financial strength, artists and reputations.
- Allow players to purchase smaller record labels or negotiate complete company acquisitions.

## Objective
- Expand the existing Music Empire game with interconnected publishing, music-video production, record-label acquisition, and dynamic AI industry systems while preserving current gameplay and player progression.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game; do not remove or break existing features, artists, finances, saves, or progression.
- Make the new systems functional and interconnected, including recurring income, staff, upgrades, contracts, acquisitions, and AI-driven activity.
- Add an industry intelligence section covering artists, labels, releases, trends, deals, and chart movements.
- Preserve the hybrid 2D/3D style, mobile-friendly management UI, and smooth performance.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing vanilla JavaScript app and save model; preserve and migrate legacy saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and smoke-tested the earlier studio, collectibles, awards, festivals, artist-career, and meeting expansion.
- Festival lifecycle audit passed; save restoration was verified after correcting the audit method.
- Syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed for the existing expansion changes.

### Active
- Implement the newly requested publishing company, video production company, label acquisitions/corporate expansion, and more dynamic AI industry in the existing game.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current game structure and existing uncommitted changes before extending it.
2. Plan compatible save migrations and implement the requested systems in small, integrated pieces.
3. Add mobile-friendly navigation/views/actions and production/publishing/corporate visual environments.
4. Test lifecycle/economy integration, save migration/preservation, feature screens, and mobile layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: Save migration, simulation, economy, festivals, careers, and expansion logic.
- `js/ui.js`: Navigation, feature views, modals, and action handlers.
- `js/data.js`: Game datasets and definitions.
- `js/scene3d.js`: Canvas environments.
- `js/visuals.js`: SVG icons.
- `css/styles.css`: Responsive feature styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/smoke.mjs`: Browser smoke-test harness.
- `/tmp/opencode/festival-audit.mjs`: Festival lifecycle and save-restoration audit.

## Important Context
- Existing expansion changes remain uncommitted: modified `css/styles.css`, `js/data.js`, `js/game.js`, `js/ui.js`; untracked `js/scene3d.js`, `js/visuals.js`.
- Save key: `music-empire-save-v1`; legacy-save migration was previously smoke-tested.
- Festival audit validated completion rewards and rejected booking/upgrades after completion; save restoration passes when tested without triggering a reload-time `beforeunload` overwrite.

## Objective
- Expand Music Empire with integrated publishing, music-video production, record-label acquisitions/corporate growth, and dynamic AI industry systems while preserving existing gameplay and progression.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing features, artists, finances, saves, and progression; migrate legacy saves compatibly.
- Integrate new systems with the existing economy and industry intelligence.
- Maintain the hybrid 2D/3D style, mobile-friendly management UI, and smooth performance.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing vanilla JavaScript app and save model rather than replacing core systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Earlier studio, collectibles, awards, festivals, artist-career, and meeting expansions were implemented and smoke-tested.
- Festival lifecycle and save-restoration audit passed after correcting the audit method.

### Active
- Inspect existing changes and implement publishing, video production, acquisitions/corporate expansion, and dynamic AI industry.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current navigation, state, week simulation, and uncommitted changes.
2. Implement compatible state/save migrations and economy-integrated systems in small pieces.
3. Add mobile-friendly navigation, views, actions, and relevant environments.
4. Test feature lifecycles, economy integration, save preservation/migration, screens, and mobile layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: Save migration, simulation, economy, competitors, acquisition logic, and expansion systems.
- `js/ui.js`: Navigation, feature views, modals, and action handlers.
- `js/data.js`: Game datasets and definitions.
- `js/scene3d.js`: Canvas environments.
- `js/visuals.js`: SVG icons.
- `css/styles.css`: Responsive feature styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/smoke.mjs`: Browser smoke-test harness.
- `/tmp/opencode/festival-audit.mjs`: Festival lifecycle and save-restoration audit.

## Important Context
- Existing expansion changes are uncommitted: modified `css/styles.css`, `js/data.js`, `js/game.js`, `js/ui.js`; untracked `js/scene3d.js`, `js/visuals.js`.
- Save key: `music-empire-save-v1`; legacy-save migration was smoke-tested.
- Competitors are represented in `state.competitors`; `advanceWeek()` is in `js/game.js`.
- `ui.js` has screens including `industry`, `company`, and `festivals`; screen routing is in `screenHTML()`.
- `acquireLabel(compId)` already exists in `js/game.js`, gated at tier 2 and charging based on competitor reputation and roster size.
- Earlier `git diff --check` and syntax checks passed for the existing expansion changes.
